BMW's New X5 Gets a Mild Tuning Job in Fantasy Land
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik
Unless you’ve been living under a rock these past few months, completely cut off from the car world, then you know that BMW has an entirely new X5 (among other things) in its lineup.
The fifth generation hit the assembly line in August at the Spartanburg factory in the United States of America, and it also has a long wheelbase sibling, the G78, which comes to life in China, at the Dadong facility in Shenyang, for the local market. The G65 is based on an updated version of the old model’s CLAR construction, so despite looking entirely new, it shares many traits with its predecessor, though you cannot see them at first glance.
If you are familiar with BMW’s Neue Klasse design language, then you know why the new-gen X5 looks the way it does. And here, we are talking about the design of the kidney grille, which some say is a joke, whereas others definitely like. The same goes for the new X-shaped headlights, and the aggressive design of the front bumper, with its large air intake in the middle, separated in half by a pair of vertical slats, and the vents flanking it on the outer edges, and on the outer parts of the bumper.
Did you think that the profile is not controversial at all? In that case, you clearly haven’t heard that instead of traditional door handles, or even flush-mounted ones, the new-gen BMW X5 has some winglets. As a result, the doors look cleaner overall, at least on the upper sections, because the lower parts are on the sharp-looking side of things, just like the side skirts. And for whatever reason, BMW decided to add some angular-styled lines around the wheel arches.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik The back end design is also Neue Klasse , with its new taillight signature, aggressive rear bumper, and different tailgate, which, by the way, has lost its split-opening party trick. And the cockpit is also controversial due to the addition of the Panoramic iDrive. That’s the display that stretches from one pillar to the other at the bottom of the windshield. And it’s joined by a free-floating infotainment screen, and an optional passenger display, as well as a four-spoke steering wheel.
Given that the all-new BMW X5 is not exactly a looker anymore, at least in some people’s eyes, and when compared to the older generations, we have seen quite a few rendering takes on it that try to make it a bit more appealing. The latest to have crossed our screens came from @kelsonik on Instagram, and they imagine the new premium mid-size crossover with some headlight tweaks, as well as new wheels, and a few other modifications.
Mind you, while the headlights of this rendered G65 retain their size and shape, they feature yellow daytime running lights for a more aggressive stance. The trim on the grille is now black, and black is the color that was virtually applied to the car’s entire exterior. And since this color tends to hide quirky looks very nicely, as everyone knows, the end product is definitely a lot more appealing. That’s what I think, anyway.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik Before inviting you to contradict me in the comments box below, I also have to mention other virtual modifications, because the rendered BMW X5 has also been imagined with two different sets of wheels. Both have a multi-spoke design, albeit with different patterns, but one is a lot more concave than the other. Both alloy sets sport a black finish, and in one case, they brake calipers are red, whereas in the other, they’re black.
Before wrapping it up, the pixel artist has also adjusted the suspension using the same photo-editing software, so this CGI-infused new-gen BMW X5 now sits a bit closer to the ground. The front and rear bumpers, side skirts, door mirrors, roof-mounted spoiler, and everything else carry over from the real thing.
As you likely know, the Neue Klasse BMW X5 starts from $69,800 in the United States of America. This is the MSRP of the X5 40, which is the base version of the crossover. The 40 xDrive variant kicks off at $72,100, and both feature the same 3.0-liter TwinPower Turbo inline-six engine, which develops 394 hp (400 ps/294 kW). The RWD model needs 5.2 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, and the AWD one completes the sprint in 5.1 seconds.
BMW also offers the X5 50E xDrive plug-in hybrid, which combines the same inline-six with an electric motor for a total output of 483 hp (490 ps/360 kW). That’s the same as its direct predecessor, and the same goes for the 0-60 mph, which takes 4.6 seconds. However, instead of 39 miles (63 km), it can now travel up to 44 miles (71 km) on electric power alone. Pricing starts at $77,500 in this case.
Now, back to the virtually-tuned BMW X5 pictured above, do you like it more than the real one? View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)
